title: Vibe coded a historical epidemiology detective game
author: Financial-Bid-8062
selftext:
I've been working on Case Zero, a browser-based detective game where you investigate historical disease outbreaks using the scientific tools available at the time.

The first scenario takes place in 1906 New York. You have 30 days to interview witnesses, collect samples, run laboratory tests, and figure out what's causing an outbreak.

It's an early playable prototype, with more historical cases and gameplay mechanics planned.

Would love feedback on the gameplay and UI!

**Play it here:** [https://welietoyounews-tech.github.io/case-zero/](https://welietoyounews-tech.github.io/case-zero/)

comments.author: Any-Acanthisitta-776
comments.body: It’s 12 am so I can’t play it now but I followed the post so I can later. It looks cool!

comments.author: No_Entrepreneur6548
comments.body:
It seems like my goal here is to read all of the notes? Then I can take more actions after I’ve read them? This is a little confusing and since it’s not clear what you do on the screen it makes it a little hard to know why to keep playing. I would take a shot at either turning all the notes over or giving me an early guide on when I can click on other buttons on the screen. 

I love though that you’re making a game about this subject and I think it’s one of the great part of these tools!

replies.author: Financial-Bid-8062
replies.body: Thanks for playing and for the feedback! The paperwork was meant to serve as an introduction, with the other actions greyed out until it was completed, but I think there was a bug where the unread notes didn't remain greyed out. But I don't think that its really necessary, actually. I've updated the game so field investigation unlocks after Day 1 instead. You might need to press Ctrl+Shift+R to load the latest version. Really appreciate you giving it a try!

replies.author: No_Entrepreneur6548
replies.body:
That helps get to the next section. But it’s still not super clear how the items tie together to unravel the problem. You might want to rethink the office as a hub for the investigation. You might look at or have ai look at the John Snow cholera maps and try to incorporate some of these historical statistical techniques. This would give you a better visual grounding and help connect the geo spatial element of the game. 

I might even recommend that it’s played on the map not in different tabs. With you clicking on people or buildings to unravel details as you go.

replies.author: Financial-Bid-8062
replies.body: ah yes, a very famous case indeed! however, that was a widespread outbreak, this was in a single household. i will find a way to make that clearer. no geospacial component, just a man and his laboratory. but you may have given me an idea for episode 2...😉
